correctness.rationale: Measurable coordinate projection bounds each marginal distance d_i by the heterogeneous distance Δ. Expanding the averaged tensor difference gives four ordered terms of weight 1/4; both mixed terms have TV Δ by transposition, and either diagonal term has TV at most 2d_i by two-term tensor telescoping. Equivalently the four disjoint label cells have the exact weighted TV sum before the label is forgotten. For this normalization TV is half the variation norm of a probability difference; tensoring a signed measure with a probability preserves the norm, by its Jordan decomposition. These arguments require no regularity of the space. On the discrete three-point witness the only heterogeneous unmatched masses are ε at (b,b) and (a,c) in opposite laws. The positive averaged-tensor signed masses are ε at (b,b) and ε(1−ε)/4 at each of (a,b),(b,a). Thus Δ/TV_hom=2/(3−ε) tends to 2/3 through distinct pairs, proving sharpness without asserting attainment.
residual_risks: The proof and witness concern exactly two coordinates; finite grid tests are not evidence for a universal multi-coordinate optimum.
